text:
samantha: Hey folks — quick Q. I'm moving to a 1099 contract role inside Redwood next month and there's a payroll vendor migration the same week. I have an outstanding 401(k) loan (~$3,200). Do I need to pay it off before my final W-2? What happens to loan repayment if payroll vendor changes or if I'm reclassified as contractor? Any timing gotchas with the plan vendor? Thanks!

mike: Short answer: usually yes — outstanding loans after termination are treated as a distribution unless repaid. That distribution is taxable and may trigger 10% early withdrawal if under 59½. But exact timing/processing can vary by plan vendor. :thinking:

anne: @samantha we have a vendor migration window 2026-06-10 -> 2026-06-14. Final payroll for transitioning employees runs on 2026-06-12. If you want to continue loan withholding from paychecks, we need the deduction coded before final payroll cutoff. After employment ends, payroll generally cannot continue withholding.

planbot: PlanHive policy excerpt: "If employment terminates, any outstanding loan balance not repaid within 60 days of the loan default date will be treated as a taxable distribution and reported on Form 1099-R. Loans may not be rolled over to an IRA or another plan upon termination — repayment in cash is required prior to default."

david: Practical options: 1) repay full loan now (wire or ACH) to PlanHive — avoids taxable distribution. 2) Trigger final paycheck withholding by adding deduction code LOAN_REPAY to your termination payroll (need to sign authorization). 3) If neither, loan will offset and be taxable.

samantha: If I pick final paycheck withholding, what exactly should I send/payroll? Any specific fields/account numbers?

anne: Send one email to payroll@redwood with subject "LOAN REPAY AUTH - samantha" by 2026-06-09 EOD and include: 
```
Employee: samantha
LoanID: 789012
Repay method: final paycheck withholding
Amount to withhold: $3200
Auth signature: samantha (can reply to this thread)
```
I'll add the LOAN_REPAY deduction code and confirm with benefits. If the vendor migration interferes we'll process on our side but need the auth before cutoff.

mike: I opened an inquiry with PlanHive to confirm the 60-day clock and whether vendor migration pauses processing. Case #PH-2468. Will post update here. :white_check_mark:

samantha: Thanks all — I'll send the email today and also ask PlanHive if direct ACH repayment is processed faster during migrations.

planbot: Automated notice: PlanHive records show active loan 789012, balance $3,200, orig date 2024-11-20. No existing repayment plan beyond payroll withholding.

david: Also note: if you become a contractor but still paid through payroll for a short overlap (rare), we can sometimes continue withholding if HR flags it — but that's special-case and needs approval from legal + payroll.

mike: Filing follow-up: if PlanHive confirms anything different about migration grace, I'll update thread. For now treat as: repay before termination or arrange final payroll withholding before cutoff.

samantha: Great — email sent. Will report back if PlanHive offers ACH window. :wave:
